result.title: Heirloom: Carrying a Phone's Personalization Across Base-Model Generations
result.summary: On-device language models can learn a user's preferences through adapters trained on private data. However, a base-model upgrade may change the layers or vocabulary, leaving the personal adapter incompatible. Replacing it with a non-personal adapter loses much of the personalization, while retraining requires retaining the user's labeled history. We present Heirloom, a system that transfers a personal adapter to a new base model on the phone without retaining labels. Heirloom uses the old personal model as a teacher, collecting its predictions on stored unlabeled inputs, vendor-provided prompts, or prompts generated by the new base. It then unloads the old base and trains an adapter for the new model to match those predictions, keeping only one base model in memory at a time. We evaluate Heirloom across three generation upgrades from two model families, an architecture-preserving refresh, and three personalization tasks. On movie tagging, migration from stored inputs maintains pre-upgrade accuracy and differs from labeled retraining by at most 1.7 percentage points across the three upgrades. On a phone's neural processing unit (NPU), a fixed-length migration for the 4B upgrade takes 38 minutes and consumes 20% of the battery end to end, making the stored-input setting feasible during overnight charging.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Heirloom 系统，在手机上把用户的个性化 adapter 迁移到换代后的新基座模型：以旧个人模型为教师，在无标签输入、厂商提示或新模型自生成提示上收集预测，再卸载旧基座、训练新 adapter 去拟合这些预测，从而不保留标注历史。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「用旧模型预测作无标签监督、只驻留单一基座」的做法，可能为 LVR 中跨模型版本保留潜在推理能力及无标注轨迹监督提供可供核查的思路。
